name: Automotive clay modelling
summary: A designer shapes a full-size car in warm industrial clay over a frame. The clay is cut, smoothed and checked in light before any metal is made.
how: Build a wood and foam frame in the size of the car.
Warm the clay and press it onto the frame, then cut it with rakes and scrapers.
Check the highlights in light and measure the form for the dies.

origin.note: Harley Earl's styling section at General Motors uses clay to shape cars before the steel is cut.

adoptions.via: The fin and the wrap-around glass are first judged in clay.
Stylists check the long bonnet and the short deck in clay at full size.
Designers cut the flat planes and the sharp crease of the wedge in clay.
Designers model round, soft forms in clay for the small city car.
Designers copy the old forms in clay and then scale them up.
